persons.note: A CONTEMPORARY CHICAGO PAPER OF 1833-1835 PRINTS THIS PERSON BY NAME IN THE TOWN. Read from directory_1843, newspaper_1833_1835, poll_1834. FERGUS 1839'S LATER LISTS — 1837 AND 1839 EVIDENCE, NEVER AN 1835 FACT. Fergus' Chicago Directory for 1839 names this person 1 time in its two later lists: the poll of Chicago's first city election, 2 May 1837 — “Silas W. Sherman” (f1839_v0213, printed page 42, ward 2, voting for William B. Ogden). What a match may carry, and it is short: that the man was in Chicago on 2 May 1837 and in that ward. It is written as 1837 evidence with describes_date 1837-05-02, never as an 1835 fact, and the person's grade does not move on this alone. Under the ratified ladder a second contemporary source is what lifts projected_resident, and a poll twenty-two months after the scene date is a second source about CONTINUED RESIDENCE, not about July 1835. The ward is a location in the CITY of 1837, whose six wards are drawn on printed page 46; it is not a location in the town of 1835 and does not place a house. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: Surname 'Sherman' folds to the same string as the 1837 entry's, and the given name of both begins S. (data/research/directories/fergus_1839_election_crosswalk_1835.json and fergus_1839_register_crosswalk_1835.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a poll twenty-two months after the scene date — or a register four years after it — is a second source about CONTINUED RESIDENCE rather than about July 1835. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict. THE FEDERAL LAND TRACT SALES — A PURCHASE, AND NEVER A RESIDENCE. The Illinois State Archives' Public Domain Land Tract Sales register enters this person 2 times, as “SHERMAN SILAS W”, “SHERMAN S W”, 1833-10-24 to 1836-06-22: 1 lot in the platted town — lot 8 of block 34 in the town the register codes CHIOT (L8BL34CHIOT, as printed) and 1 parcel of the school section — BL98 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E), as read, 3.27 acres stated in all, for $9697.00 (ls0331, ls1452). THE REGISTER'S OWN RESIDENCE COLUMN READS UNKNOWN on these rows: a county, a state or nothing, and never a town, which is why a purchase here places nobody. THE SCHOOL-SECTION ROWS ARE GROUND INSIDE THE TOWN, NOT FARMLAND: section 16 of T39N R14E was platted and sold off by lot and by block at the sale of 1833, which is why the register states 0000.00 acres against most of them. Ground inside the town is nearer to this reconstruction than a quarter-section is, and it is still a purchase: the register names a purchaser and never an occupant, and nothing here puts this person on that ground. THE TOWN LOTS ARE THE PLAT ITSELF, AND THEY ARE NOT ACRES: Cook County's register describes them by lot and block in a platted town and gives them no section, no township and no acreage at all, so they add nothing to the acre figure above and $9500.00 to the money. This project does not expand the register's town codes, so which addition a lot stands in is carried as the code and not as a name. It is still a purchase and it still places nobody. A purchase and nothing more. It dates and places a transaction; it proposes no residence, and under the ratified ladder it corroborates rather than mints. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: SHERMAN SILAS W matches Silas W Sherman: the forename names Silas W Sherman of the 4 people of this surname, and the forename agrees in full. (data/research/land_sales/resident_crosswalk.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a land entry is a second source about a TRANSACTION rather than about who was living at Chicago on 1 July 1835 — a man may buy a quarter-section he never sees. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict. THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 1 time: Election returns — poll list of 1834, filed 11 August 1834 — “Sherman, Silas W.” (poll_1834_099, line 268). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: one resident of the surname 'Sherman' agrees with the entry's forenames; 4 bearer(s) of the surname were considered. (data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json).

persons.name: John Wright
persons.note: ONE OF THE TWELVE WHO VOTED FOR INCORPORATION on 5 August 1833 (Andreas prints the poll: 'John W. Wright'), one of the twenty-eight electors five days later, a candidate who took two votes, and one of the nine village citizens founding the First Presbyterian Church on 26 June 1833 and one of its three first elders. Charles Butler met him on his first morning in Chicago in August 1833, at the funeral of a child. The Chicago Democrat of 26 November 1833 is the only contemporary Chicago document this project holds, and an advertisement in it is a peculiarly good witness: the advertiser was paying for it and his customers had to be able to find him. It is also NINETEEN MONTHS before the scene date, in the town's fastest-changing period, so it is strong evidence of existence and address in November 1833 and weak evidence of survival to 1 July 1835.

persons.name: John S. Wright
persons.note: A MINOR IN 1833 AND A FOUNDING MEMBER OF THE FIRST PRESBYTERIAN CHURCH IN JUNE OF THAT YEAR - his name is in the list of nine village citizens alongside his father's. He would have been about twenty in 1835. THE RELATIONSHIP IS THIS RECORD'S READING: Andreas lists the two Wrights separately and never says they are father and son, and 'John Wright, came in 1832, a merchant' and 'John S. Wright, then a minor ... came in 1832' arriving in the same year with the same surname and joining the same church on the same day is a strong reading and not a statement.
